spans.s: AF0178 अमर्त्य amartya More than one's natural capacity, Imperishable, Immortal

SV0026 अमात्रावत् आहार amātrāvat āhāra Taking inappropriate quantity of food is of two types - deficient and excessive. Food in deficient quantity is said to be causing loss of strength, complexion & development, unsaturation, upward movement of vayu, harms the lifespan, virility, immunity etc food in excessive vitiating all dosa's. fainting, giddiness, irregularity of digestion, stiffness of flanks etc.
AF0173 अमानुष amānuṣa Unprecedented, Unmaly or Super power

SK0006 आम āma 1. Raw, uncooked, unbaked, immature, unripe 2. May be associated with food or other physiological entities to mean incomplete transformation or metabolism causing a harmful effect on health.
AF0024 आम पुरीषम् āma purīṣam Stools which are undigested, immature, not formed
AF0025 आमगङ्ध āmagaṅdha Smell of raw flesh
SR0004 आमपक्वाषयः āmapakvāṣayaḥ gastro-intestinal tract - The digestive tube from stomach and intestines
BK0006 आमपाक āmapāka The initial partially cooked stage of processing of oil/ ghee, which is not useful for therapeutics
AF0027 आममत्स्यगङ्ध āmamatsyagaṅdha smell of live fish
AF0026 आमलपाङ्दु āmalapāṅdu Color of pale myrobalan

AT0003 आमविश āmaviśa It is a kind of disorder which results from incompatible food or from eating before digestion of previous meals, similar to intestinal toxemia because it simulates the symptoms of toxemia.
BP0241 आमान्य-विशेष सिद्धान्त āmānya-viśeṣa siddhānta An applied principle of āyurveda which is used for maintaining the equilibrium of the body constituent; Doctrine of similar and Opposites
SR0003 आमाशयः āmāśayaḥ Stomach -A dilated sac like distensible portion of alimentary canal between the esophagus and the duodenum which contains partially digested food. It is a major seat of Pitta.
